restrictions: The two messages have 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 bytes for one t with 1 <= t < 2^32: t zero chunks of 1024 bytes followed by a last chunk of one block. The last chunk is compressed as a non-root chunk with counter t (v12 = t, v13 = 0), flags 3 and its true block length; the 63-byte block ends in eight zero bytes, so words 14 and 15 and the top byte of word 13 are zero in both zero-filled blocks. Equal last-chunk chaining values give equal digests by the tree lemma of proof.md Section 7.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.

Exact part: for every trial of proof.md Section 8 the two last-chunk chaining values agree on words 0, 2, 5 and 7, E1.c1 lies in the cube of beta* = 18b0e098 so that beta = beta* in every trial, Y4 ranges over the whole class of eta (524,288 values; no sub-class, no rule on h1), and the counter t is solved per trial as ROL(K0.d1,16) XOR K0.a1; trials with t = 0 are skipped. The search continues only in outer steps that pass the exact filter of proof.md Section 8 for the six listed E1 outcomes S = {175,185,275,285,385,685}020a0 (share 279,070,422,111 / 2^48 = 2^-9.9782); of these, the joint solver sees only those kept by the exact s-pattern pre-check, and its guards (G7) and (G15) drop only words that hold no success, so by Lemmas F, VP, G7 and G15 none of these steps loses a counted success. The eight other outcomes of beta* are not counted as successes.

Heuristic part: under H1', H4' and H5', each stated for the advice record of proof.md Section 12, with probability at least 0.39 the search finds a trial whose remaining 128 chaining-value bits also agree. It walks 2^90.465 trials: 2^50.465 contexts (proof.md 9.8), each the seven outer words of one fresh draw, times the 2^19 members of the class, times the 2^21 trials of an outer step.

Machine: a classical word RAM with 256-bit words under collision-frontier-v5, 430 machine units (operations, loads, stores) to the unit, 64 registers and constants as immediates; fetching a word from memory is a load. Charges (proof.md 9.8, 11; GPT Sol answer CD): 600 units per context, which draws its fresh word and runs the 39 member-free lines of step CO once; 67 units per batch of seven members in packed 36-bit lanes (43 for the last batch of three partners of a cluster), which computes the 8 member lines on which omega depends and omega and tests every lane against the direct table T2; and 64 units for each lane whose test-(2) mask meets S, which updates the E count, held in a register, in three operations, computes the 17 lines on which only Y9 depends in 16 packed lines and tests against T1. Participant programs executed and counted the batch of 67 and this Q path in its earlier form of 78; the organizer does not run them.

Cluster gate (proof.md 9.9, Lemmas KP, A9, CL and OR; GPT Sol answers CI 1 and CJ 1): the 32 members that differ only in bits 10 to 14 of e1 form a cluster, and all have omega mod 2^9 in two values computed from the representative; a fixed table P of 2^21 words (built once, 2^27 units charged) skips the cluster when neither value can pass test (2), so every skipped member fails test (2) and no success, count or credit debit is lost. Charges: 118 units per batch of seven representatives (the batch of 67, a gate key of 10 and seven gate tests of 41; 82 for the last of a context; 2,341 per context) and 375 per opened cluster (five partner batches, 4 * 67 + 43, and 64 for its frame, cursor and opened count). The run halts when the opened count passes A_BUDGET = 11,711,020,335,594,018,703, and the time bound charges A_BUDGET + 1. No premise: Lemma OR proves that for uniform outer words the gate opens on at most 0.459991515 of the clusters on average, so the budget is passed with probability at most exp(-20).

Building T1 and T2, one entry per 32-bit word, costs below 2^39 units once (2^38 bytes). A passing lane is charged 462 units, its rebuild, the 29 words saved around the solver, pre-check, the three words of (G7) and its credit test included. When the pre-check keeps outcomes T, the proved cap C15(T) <= 17,504 of the joint solver with the guards (G7) and (G15), its global ledger of 1,024 and the root certificates (four one-word tests, 120 units a root) is subtracted from a prepaid credit of 2,249,200,173,638,569,939,473 units before the solver starts. These are proved upper allowances of a specified layout, not measured counts. Nothing is sorted, every word-indexed read is charged as a load, and the tables do not grow with the trials.

Halts: the run stops with failure as soon as the opened-cluster count, the test-(2) count or the pass count passes its budget, as soon as a C15(T) is larger than the credit left, and after RUN_CONTEXTS = 1,553,906,557,396,539 contexts. The time bound charges each budget plus one, RUN_CONTEXTS + 1 contexts, all 2,341 * RUN_CONTEXTS representative batches and the whole credit, so it holds for every run (proof.md Sections 9, 11).

This package is our entry 415e792c with the member loop and the direct tables of entry e9b6649e (hecmas), the guard (G7) of our entry 0bc5f130 with the credit at the exact model mean with (G7), scaled by 16/27, the omega-first batch (GPT Sol, answer CA, its charges audited in answer CD), and the E count in a register, the root certificate, the guard (G15), the global ledger of 1,024 (GPT Sol, answers CD 8, 10 and 11 and CF 6 and 7) and the cluster gate (answers CI 1 and CJ 1). Randomness: one fresh uniform 256-bit word per context. Since each context visits each member of the class once or skips it in a cluster that fails test (2) (Lemmas CX and CL), means over outer steps equal those of a uniform outer step; independence, however, holds between contexts only, as the 2^19 outer steps of a context share its words. H1' (ii) is therefore stated per context, which is stronger than a per-step clause. Success 0.39 holds only under H1', H4' and H5'.

The factor 98,937,639,497 in H1' is five sevenths of the model's conditional count of the six listed outcomes on the class, rounded down, and is not measured by the organizer-run experiments, which run the root instance (counter 0, flags 11): no digest experiment can show a half-collision of a non-root chunk's chaining value. The cluster gate, the filter, the pre-check, (G7) and (G15) lose nothing; the two count shares matter only for the budgets (H4') and the mean of C(T) with (G7) only for the credit (H5'). No full 2-round collision is exhibited.

The submitted program is that of entry 26ebba63, unchanged (the earlier sub-class search, its own constants); it does not run the member loop, the direct tables, the omega-first batch, the cluster gate, the pre-check, the guards (G7) and (G15), the root certificate or the credit. All of these, with the outcome set, the budgets, the solver layout and the certificate, exist in proof.md only. The participant programs cited in proof.md 9.8 and Section 13 (checks of the member loop and of the omega-first batch up to the pass decision, the clustering measurement and the measurements of the gate) are not part of the package.

Fixed nonuniform advice, stated in full in proof.md Section 12: the six 32-bit constants of 3.2, eta = 830303cf, beta* = 18b0e098 with the mask 0e09818b and value 02008000 of its cube, the seven tau values and eps = 6e21be55 of the filter's automata and the mask 5f of S, 73 bytes that the search reads, and 20 bytes of the root instance, 93 bytes in all (nonuniform_advice_log2_bytes 7). The success analysis uses only properties of this stated record that proof.md verifies exactly: Fact P (3.2), Lemma Q, Theorem C (iii) and (iv), the table of 10.1 with the program of Section 17, the certificate of the filter for S (Section 8), and the pre-check patterns and solver guards, trees and caps for this class (9.4, 9.7, 11). H1', H4' and H5' are stated for this record and none concerns how it was found; no premise concerns what any selection returns. The selection procedure SEL that found it is charged in full as preprocessing (preprocessing_log2).

preprocessing_log2 55, included in time_log2, is the charge of the selection procedure SEL of proof.md Section 12, which found the advice: 116 solver runs capped at 2^56 operations each, one count per model capped at 2^52 (+ 2^10), and the choice of S capped at 2^50, in all S_old = 8,882,224,365,081,579,520 operations, below 2^62.946, below 2^54.198 units, rounded up to 55. The cap holds by construction, since every run halts at its cap; that SEL returns exactly the stored values rests on the participant's solver log and recounts, which are not in the package. The cost model charges any search omitted from the submitted program; SEL is that search, and its whole capped cost is charged. The search alone is below 2^64.4022 units. memory_log2_bytes 44 covers, all held at once (sum below 2^44), the two output messages (each below 2^42 bytes), the search with its code and direct tables (below 2^39 bytes) and every run of SEL (below 2^34 + 2^20 bytes). No priority or novelty claim is made.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. Stated for the instance that the advice record of proof.md Section 12 fixes, and for no other. The run has RUN_CONTEXTS independent contexts, each the seven outer words of one fresh uniform 256-bit word, and every context visits all 2^19 members of the class, except the members of clusters that the gate of proof.md 9.9 skips, which fail test (2) and hold no listed good trial (Lemmas CX and CL). Let N_o be the number of listed good valid trials of one outer step (t != 0, R = 0, and an E1 outcome in S = {175,185,275,285,385,685}020a0, six outcomes of beta*; Y4 in the whole class of eta; no rule on h1), counted over all of Q* whether or not the outer step passes the filter or the pre-check, and N_c its sum over the 2^19 outer steps of a context. (i) For a uniform outer step U (seven uniform outer words, a uniform member), E[N_o(U)] >= (2^21 - 1) q with q = FACTOR * 2^-128, FACTOR = floor(5 * 138,512,695,296 / 7) = 98,937,639,497, about 2^-91.474 (just under five sevenths of the conditional model rate p of Lemma S1 for S); by Lemma CX (c), E[N_c] = 2^19 E[N_o(U)], so (i) is the statement of entry 415e792c. (ii) With the context as the unit, as entry e9b6649e declares it: the probability that no valid trial of the run is a listed good trial is at most exp(-0.49676) + 0.001; that is, listed good trials are not clustered, neither among the trials of one outer step nor among the outer steps (members) of one context, beyond what this bound allows. Given (i), rho_c = E[N_c(N_c-1)]/E[N_c] <= 0.0065 is sufficient for (ii) by Lemma S8 applied to the independent contexts. rho_c = rho_w + rho_x, where rho_w is the per-step factorial ratio of entry 415e792c and rho_x >= 0 the part that pairs of different members of one context add, so this clause is stronger than the per-step clause of entry 415e792c. Part (ii) is an assumption: rho_c is not measured and cannot be measured at full size (proof.md 10.3). This restates the rate-and-dependence premise of entry 26ebba63 for the whole class, S and the walk by contexts; that entry's clause was for the sub-class of 2^17 members with rule A and seven outcomes and does not by itself imply this law (GPT Sol, answer AT 2). It is declared here anew. By Lemma F every listed good trial lies in an outer step that passes the filter, by Lemma CL the cluster gate skips none, by Lemma VP the pre-check skips none and by Lemmas G7 and G15 the guards (G7) and (G15) drop none, so N_o is the same count, pointwise (GPT Sol, answer AW 1).
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Sections 8 and 9: lengths 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 with a non-root last chunk (counter t, v13 = 0, flags 3), the six constants of Section 3.2, Y4 ranging over all 524,288 members of the class of eta (Lemma Q) inside every context, a context being the seven outer words of one fresh 256-bit word of the run (proof.md 9.8, Lemma CX); in every trial E1.c1 is drawn from the cube of beta* = 18b0e098, and t is solved per trial, with t = 0 skipped. The search continues only in outer steps that pass the exact filter of Section 8 for S, the solver sees only those that the pre-check of 9.7 keeps, and it applies the guards (G7) and (G15); N_o counts all of Q* in every outer step and only the six outcomes of S.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the participant's exact count, in integer arithmetic under the seven-word model of Section 10 with Y4 uniform in the class, of the part of beta* on the class carried by the six outcomes of S (67,633,152 = 1,032 * 2^16 on the per-trial scale 2^-83 of the class; the counting program and the six rows of its output are printed in Section 17), times 2^11 for drawing E1.c1 from the cube (Lemma S1), taken at five sevenths, rounded down. The filter, the pre-check, (G7) and (G15) change neither the count nor the premise (Lemmas S9 (b), VP, G7 and G15). Participant evidence of Section 13, untrusted by the harness: a whole-class graphics-card run of 2^46 real counter trials in 2^25 passing outer steps, with a sub-class control of the same size, in which every measured quantity matches the exact model within 1.5 clustered standard errors, among them the E1 rate on the whole class of the seven outcomes of entry 59f8915e, 1.0020 +- 0.0086 of the model (13,595 events), and its ratio to the sub-class rate, 0.9895 +- 0.0120 (model 1); the E1 event of S is a sub-event of that measured event (52/53 of it in the model); and a reduced-width (8-bit) end-to-end run of complete messages, with no sub-class and no rule, in which the counter arrangement found 251 collisions against 255.0 predicted. At 32 bits the joint 128-bit event itself, about 2^-91 per trial, is not measured. Dependence (proof.md 10.3 and Section 13, participant runs on the counter instance made after the design): part (ii) is assumed, not measured. Under the model E[N_c] is about 2^-51.474, and rho_x is about v * E[N_c], where v is the clustering ratio of listed good trials by context (1 for independent members); so (ii) fails only if v exceeds about 2^44, or if one listed good trial makes another in the same context far more likely than its rate. Evidence that v is near 1: the same ratio, (E[n(n-1)]/E[n]) / ((2^19 - 1) p_hat) for per-context counts of events that every listed good trial meets, is 1.1513 for the filter pass, 1.1572 for the pass with the pre-check and 1.153 for an outer step whose solver reaches a leaf (120,000 contexts; control arms of independent outer steps 1.0000, 1.0000 and 0.998), and 1.2486 +- 0.0806 for an outer step whose solver returns a root (46,104,576 contexts; control 1.0367 +- 0.0718); it does not grow with depth beyond the errors. The clustering comes from condition (2), whose omega has w8 fixed by the context. Preregistered (proof.md Section 13; 262,144 contexts and 2^46 trials per arm, two generators, a control arm): the cross-member factor Rx is 0.999 +- 0.054 (upper limit 1.162) for the listed E1 outcome, 2^-32.29 per trial, 0.90 +- 0.24 (upper limit 1.94) for (J1) and (J2) of the E3 half, 2^-34.58, and 1.0002 for R24, 2^-23.76; only the filter events cluster (1.144, 1.152); every upper limit lies at least 43 bits below the 2^44.21 that the clause allows.
heuristics.limitations: The factor 98,937,639,497 is assumed (five sevenths of the model count of the six outcomes of S on the class, rounded down). The premise of entry 26ebba63 was for the sub-class with rule A; it is not inherited, and the whole-class law of N_o for S is declared, not proved. The organizer-run experiments run the root instance (counter 0, flags 11) of the same construction and measure neither the factor nor the counter half-collision, which no digest experiment can show. Part of the transfer of the single-trial law to the actual sampler is proved (Lemmas S1-S5, S8, S9, VP, G7 and G15) and part is assumed in (i). Part (ii) is an assumption: the bound rho_c <= 0.0065 is not measured and cannot be measured at full size, since a context holds a listed good trial with probability about 2^-51.474; the proved cap of 16 listed good trials in one outer step (Lemmas CV, G7 and G15) does not help at this run length. Stated for contexts, it is stronger than a per-step clause, since it adds the cross-member part rho_x. The clustering ratios that support it are measured for events that every listed good trial meets, from the filter to the roots of the solver (one generator, after the design) and, preregistered with two generators, the two halves of a listed good trial, not for listed good trials: the joint event, about 2^-91 per trial, is not reachable, so carrying Rx near 1 to it remains the premise. The whole-class graphics-card run measures the E1 side of the seven outcomes together and the filter, not the six of S on their own, not the E3 side nor the joint event. Lemmas F, VP, G7, G15 and S9 (a) use no law of the words; the 8-bit end-to-end run has no filter. The counter-instance member loop is specified in proof.md and is not executed by the submitted program.

heuristics.statement: Supporting; stated for the advice record of proof.md Section 12. Two count-budget clauses with one failure allowance for their union: with probability at least 0.9995 over the coins both hold, and then no budget halts the run. (a) Pass budget: no more than PASS_BUDGET = 858,218,304,486,124,637 outer steps pass the filter for S, whose nominal share is pi = 279,070,422,111 / 2^48 = 2^-9.9782. (b) Test-(2) budget: no more than E_BUDGET = 47,103,299,361,697,989,262 lanes run the Q path because their test-(2) mask meets S, with nominal share 233,715,456 / 2^32 = 2^-4.1998. Each budget is ceil(17/16 * RUN_STEPS * share), with RUN_STEPS = 814,694,561,164,316,639,232 = 2^19 * RUN_CONTEXTS. Reaching a budget halts with failure; the time bound charges each budget plus one. Both counts add up independent per-context counts, each between 0 and 2^19 (Lemma CX). Provided that, for a uniform outer step, each indicator has probability at most 1.06 times its nominal share, Bernstein's inequality over the contexts bounds each overflow by exp(-3 RUN_STEPS p / (2^20 * 509,200)), that is below exp(-2.4 * 10^8) for (b) and exp(-4.5 * 10^6) for (a), far below 0.0005 together. The number of outer steps that reach the solver has no budget and no clause here: the solver is paid from the credit of H5prime-weighted-solver-work (GPT Sol, answer AW 5).
heuristics.scope: The counts N_E and N_2 of proof.md 10.3, taken over all RUN_STEPS outer steps, every member of every context (9.1, 9.8): per context, each count lies between 0 and 2^19, the contexts are independent, and the mean per context is 2^19 times the indicator's probability for a uniform outer step (Lemma CX (c)); the two indicators of one outer step may depend on each other in any way.
heuristics.extrapolation: The nominal shares are exact for uniform independent (Y9, omega) (GPT Sol, answers AC, AN and AW 3; the certificate of Section 8). Measured (Section 13, untrusted by the harness, whole class): on 60,000,000 real outer steps from Python's generator the two counts are 1.0004 +- 0.0005 (test (2)) and 0.9980 +- 0.0041 (pass) of their nominal values; on another 30,000,000 the pass count is 0.9981 +- 0.0058 of its nominal value. With the member loop, one SplitMix64 run of 120,000 contexts with all 2^19 members each: pass share 0.99847 and test-(2) share 0.99868 of nominal, z = -1.36 and -1.21 against the standard errors of the per-context counts. On 2^35 outer steps of the sub-class, with the seven-outcome filter, the pass share was 1.00012 +- 0.00016 of its exact value.
heuristics.limitations: The bound of 1.06 times the nominal share on each indicator's probability is not proved: Y9 and omega are not proved independent and uniform. The measurements are runs of generators made after the design, not a locked validation. Over contexts the tails are weaker than over independent outer steps and still far below 0.0005 (exp(-4.5 * 10^6) for the pass count). The time bound, the filter and the pre-check do not depend on these shares.

heuristics.statement: Supporting; stated for the advice record of proof.md Section 12. This is the premise H4-AS-v-S(eps) of GPT Sol's answer AW 5, E_phys[V_S(U)] <= (1+eps) * cbar_S, taken at eps = 0.06 for the caps with the guard (G7) of answer AX 1. For an outer step U of the run, before any halt, let V(U) = C(T(U)), where T = X AND VMASK[nu] is the set of outcomes that the pre-check of proof.md 9.7 keeps and C is the proved (G7) cap of steps 2 and 3 on those outcomes (4,096 + 2,304 F + 1,280 A + 20 N_f + 48 N_r + 4 N_s + 368 Lf over the rows of T with their trees with (G7), Section 11; at most 31,456), with V(U) = 0 when T is empty or the step does not pass the filter; V(U) is at least 27/16 times the cap C15(T) that the run debits (guard (G15), the root certificate and the global ledger, Section 11). Premise: for a uniform outer step, and hence for the mean over the outer steps of one context (Lemma CX (c)), the mean E[V(U)] is at most 1.06 * cbar, where cbar = 582,173,006,981,436 / 2^47 = 4.136588... is the exact mean of V in the counting model. This is a single weighted moment over all outer steps, the zeros counted; it is not a mean of executed work, because V bounds the work of steps 2 and 3 in every outer step. Use: the run debits C15(T) <= 16/27 C(T) before steps 2 and 3 from a credit that starts at CREDIT = ceil(16/27 * 17/16 * RUN_STEPS * 1.06 * cbar) = 2,249,200,173,638,569,939,473, and it halts with failure when C15(T) exceeds what is left, so the credit is exhausted only when the run total of V exceeds 17/16 * RUN_STEPS * 1.06 * cbar; the per-context sums of V are independent and lie between 0 and 2^19 * 31,456, and the Bernstein inequality over contexts puts the probability that the credit is exhausted below exp(-4.1 * 10^8). The time bound charges the whole credit whether or not the premise holds; success 0.39 holds under H1', H4' and this premise (proof.md 10.3, 10.4).
heuristics.scope: V(U) for every one of the RUN_STEPS outer steps of proof.md 9.1, that is, for every member of every one of the RUN_CONTEXTS contexts (9.8), as a function of the context's outer words and the member, with S = 0x5f, the masks X of the filter of Section 8, nu by formula (V) of 9.7 and the caps with (G7) of Section 11; the mean is over all outer steps, passing or not.
heuristics.extrapolation: cbar is exact in the counting model M_v of proof.md 10.3 (uniform independent (Y9, omega) and an independent uniform three-bit nu): CBAR = 582,173,006,981,436 is an eighth of the sum of n_X C(X) over the ten masks X of S that occur, 4,657,384,055,851,488, recounted by the participant in integers from the certificate of Section 8 and the trees with (G7); without (G7) the same sum gives 611,713,706,062,329. Measured, untrusted by the harness: the participant's preregistered sample (PREREG.txt SHA-256 92d16cda1cd13aacb287470b968ff2d914362b12fefb680c94960280a7471131) of 2^39 = 549,755,813,888 real outer steps of the whole class measured V with (G7): mean 4.136407 against 4.136588, ratio 0.999956 +- 0.000089, one-sided upper bounds 1.000297 (empirical Bernstein, delta 0.00135, range 31,456) and 1.000384 (bounded KL), both below 1.06, so the rule fixed in advance gives SUPPORTED at eps = 0.06. An earlier preregistered sample (PREREG.txt SHA-256 c862bfb1082e5236b0d9d81d6daef38e5f1135b27b25ad5c0093a1bf76455872) of 2^28 = 268,435,456 real outer steps measured V without (G7), with another generator: ratio 0.99456 +- 0.00405 to 4.346487, one-sided upper bounds 1.01059 and 1.01513. Since V with (G7) is at most 723/715 times V without it in every outer step, that sample bounds the mean with (G7) by 1.0786 times cbar.
heuristics.limitations: Not proved: the sampler's nu is a function of the outer step and is not proved uniform or independent of the masks, so cbar is not a property of the sampler. Support at eps = 0.06 rests on the model value and on one preregistered sample from one pseudorandom generator (Philox4x32-10), run by the participant outside the organizer's harness on the counter instance that no organizer experiment runs; V is the proved cap C(T), not executed work, and the sample tests neither H1' nor H4'. If the premise fails, the credit can halt the run with failure, which lowers the success probability and not the time bound. This premise takes the place of the third count budget of our entry 0bc5f130.
